fixes.find: A whole-home humidifier mounts on the furnace plenum or the return duct, not in one room. A small water line feeds a wet panel or a rotating drum. Warm furnace air passes across that media, and the moisture travels through the ducts that already carry heat. A humidistat and a low-voltage transformer wire into the furnace board, so the unit runs only while the blower runs. A flow-through panel unit also needs a pitched drain for the water the media does not absorb; a drum unit instead holds water in a reservoir that needs cleaning. Because the tie-in is to the duct system, the whole house gains moisture and nothing sits in the living space.
fixes.replace: A whole-home humidifier mounts on the furnace plenum or the return duct, not in one room. Evaporative models use a small water line to feed a wet panel or a rotating drum, and warm furnace air passes across that media. Steam models boil water in their own canister and inject steam into the duct, so they need a dedicated electrical circuit and do not rely on warm furnace air. Water, drain and control needs depend on the product: a flow-through panel needs a pitched drain, a drum holds water in a reservoir that needs cleaning, and a steam canister needs draining or flushing. Because the tie-in is to the duct system, the whole house gains moisture and nothing sits in the living space.
fixes.why: MAJOR: answer explained only evaporative designs; added steam humidifiers and product-dependent water/control requirements

fixes.find: Cold outdoor air holds very little moisture. A forced-air furnace heats that air without putting any back.
fixes.replace: Cold outdoor air holds very little moisture. When a furnace warms that air, its relative humidity drops, even though no water is removed. How dry the house gets depends on how much outdoor air leaks in and how much moisture cooking, bathing and occupants add.
fixes.why: MAJOR: explain that heating lowers relative humidity; infiltration and moisture sources set the load

fixes.find: Accessory work is not the same thing as an equipment replacement. A humidifier or a filter cabinet tied into existing ducts replaces no appliance. City of Chicago permit records bear that out. The permits on file describe equipment replacements, including furnaces and heat pumps, rather than accessory tie-ins to a system that stays in place. Where a dedicated circuit or a plumbing change forms part of the job, the trade involved decides what is required. City & Suburban confirms what the specific job requires before work starts, and prices upfront with no hidden fees.
fixes.replace: Accessory work is not the same thing as an equipment replacement, but that alone does not make it permit-exempt. City of Chicago permit records on file mostly describe equipment replacements, including furnaces and heat pumps, and a sample of records cannot show what a specific accessory job requires. A dedicated circuit, a plumbing change or a new duct opening can each change the answer. Confirm the requirement for the specific scope with the City of Chicago and the responsible trade before work starts. City & Suburban prices upfront with no hidden fees.
fixes.why: CRITICAL: permit determination is not a company practice; no exemption inferred from permit-record sample
